# EDA Findings

*Generated by `src/eda.py` from the MySQL database `restaurant_intelligence`. All numbers are computed at run time. Statistical tests show association, not causation.*

## Key figures

- Restaurants: **9,551**; rated **7,403**; unrated **2,148**.
- India accounts for **90.6%** of restaurants.
- The four largest cities (New Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Faridabad) hold **82.9%** of all restaurants. Of 43 Indian cities, **39** have 25 or fewer restaurants, which suggests Zomato listed only a small sample outside Delhi NCR.
- Ratings (rated only): mean **3.44**, median 3.40, SD 0.55, skewness 0.23.
- Votes (rated only): median **60**, mean 202.2, skewness 7.95 (heavily right-skewed, so medians and rank-based tests are used).
- Most common cuisine: **North Indian**, offered by 41.5% of restaurants.

## Statistical tests

| # | Question | Test | Groups / n | Statistic | p-value | Effect size | Significant (α = 0.05) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Is rating associated with number of votes? (rated restaurants) | Spearman correlation | n=7,403 | 0.682 | < 0.001 | rho = 0.682 | Yes |
| T2 | Does rating differ across price ranges? | Kruskal-Wallis H | 4 groups, n=7,403 | 1,326.1 | < 0.001 | epsilon-squared = 0.179 | Yes |
| T3 | Is price range associated with rating? | Spearman correlation | n=7,403 | 0.402 | < 0.001 | rho = 0.402 | Yes |
| T4 | India: does rating differ with online delivery? | Mann-Whitney U | Delivery (n=2,327, median=3.40) vs No delivery (n=4,186, median=3.30) | 5,232,985.0 | < 0.001 | rank-biserial r = 0.074 | Yes |
| T5 | India: does rating differ with table booking? | Mann-Whitney U | Booking (n=1,064, median=3.60) vs No booking (n=5,449, median=3.30) | 3,730,574.5 | < 0.001 | rank-biserial r = 0.287 | Yes |
| T6 | India: is cost for two (INR) associated with rating? | Spearman correlation | n=6,504 | 0.332 | < 0.001 | rho = 0.332 | Yes |
| T7 | Is the number of cuisines offered associated with rating? | Spearman correlation | n=7,394 | 0.118 | < 0.001 | rho = 0.118 | Yes |
| T8 | Is popularity class independent of price range? | Chi-square independence | 4x3 table, n=7,403, dof=6 | 1,427.6 | < 0.001 | Cramer's V = 0.311 | Yes |
| T9 | Is popularity class independent of online delivery? | Chi-square independence | 2x3 table, n=7,403, dof=2 | 373.2 | < 0.001 | Cramer's V = 0.225 | Yes |
| T10 | Is popularity class independent of table booking? | Chi-square independence | 2x3 table, n=7,403, dof=2 | 513.0 | < 0.001 | Cramer's V = 0.263 | Yes |
| T11 | Do chain branches (2+ outlets) differ in rating from single outlets? | Mann-Whitney U | Chain (n=2,376, median=3.30) vs Single (n=5,027, median=3.40) | 5,108,139.0 | < 0.001 | rank-biserial r = -0.145 | Yes |
| T12 | India: are localities with more rated restaurants (competition) rated differently? (localities with 10+ rated) | Spearman correlation | n=161 | 0.121 | 0.126 | rho = 0.121 | No |

Effect-size guide used in interpretation (rule of thumb): |rho| or |r| < 0.1 negligible, 0.1–0.3 small, 0.3–0.5 moderate, > 0.5 large; Cramér's V < 0.1 negligible, 0.1–0.3 small, 0.3–0.5 moderate.

Online delivery vs rating, official figure (used in the report, the docs and the Power BI dashboard): **India only, rated restaurants, mean rating: 3.37 with delivery (n=2,327) vs 3.34 without (n=4,186)** (SQL Q08; T4 above reports the medians of the same groups). Delivery exists only in India and UAE, so an all-countries comparison (3.38 vs 3.47) is misleading: its 'no delivery' group also contains the 862 rated restaurants outside India without delivery, which average 4.08.
